title: Flip Columns For Maximum Number of Equal Rows
statement:
`matrix` is a grid of `m` rows and `n` columns whose cells are all `0` or `1`. You may pick any set of columns (possibly none) and invert each picked column, turning every `0` in it into `1` and every `1` into `0`.

A row is **uniform** when all of its cells hold the same value. Choose the columns so that as many rows as possible are uniform, and return that largest possible number of uniform rows.
notes:
## Intuition

Fix a set of flipped columns. Two rows both become uniform exactly when they are equal or exact complements of each other: a row that is all `0`s afterwards and a row that is all `1`s afterwards differ in every column. So the rows group into "same pattern up to complement", and the answer is the size of the largest group (flip the columns where one row of that group has a `1`). Trying every row's flip set and counting is O(m² · n); grouping with a hash map is O(m · n).

## Approach

1. Give each row a canonical key: XOR every cell with the row's first cell. A row and its complement get the same key, which always starts with `0`.
2. Count how many rows share each key in `count`.
3. The largest count, tracked in `best`, is the answer.

## Example 1, step by step

`matrix = [[0,1],[1,1]]`. Row `[0,1]` has first cell `0`, so its key is `"01"`; `count` becomes `{"01": 1}` and `best = 1`. Row `[1,1]` has first cell `1`, so its key is `"00"`; it starts a new group of size `1`. No key reaches `2`, so the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n): every cell is read once while building the keys.
- Space: O(m · n): the map may store one key of length `n` per row.

## Pitfalls

- A row and its complement must land in the same group; keying on the raw row misses Example 2.
- Rows with only one column are always uniform; the keys are all `"0"`, so the answer is `m`.
- Joining cells without a fixed width is safe here because every row has the same length and each cell is one character.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | how many rows share each canonical key |
| `best` | largest group size seen so far |
| `row` | the current row of `matrix` |
| `key` | the row XORed with its first cell, as a string |
| `total` | the size of `key`'s group including this row |

narration.14: Flipping the columns where one row of the biggest group has a 1 makes the whole group uniform.
